extracted.intended_audience: journalism students / news reporters / news-writing trainees
extracted.subtask_description: Exercises and guidance on writing and critiquing newspaper leads and short news stories, focusing on accuracy, tone, chronology, and appropriate detail for various editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include age/place/residence in leads when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the age of the person, his place of residence, or similar details necessary to an effective lead are lacking, supply them (paragraphs 100-120).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply missing age, residence, or comparable identifying details whenever they are necessary to an effective lead; add such facts rather than leaving the lead vague.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write effective, concise leads
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct such of the following leads as need correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leads should be tightened to get to the point, omit irrelevant ornamentation, and present the most important facts up front (use the examples in paragraphs 100-120 to practice rewriting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep the time relation entirely clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the following story for its excellence in keeping the time relation entirely clear. Show how the writer obtains this clearness and how he avoids the possibility of libel. (Paragraphs 124-131.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a clear chronology so readers always understand when events occurred; use explicit time markers and sequence facts logically to prevent confusion and inadvertent libelous implication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticize the following stories from the standpoint of accuracy of presentation. Rewrite the second. (Paragraphs 122-126.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check facts, avoid unfounded inferences or sensational claims, verify names/ages/places, and rewrite stories that distort or misstate events to reflect verified information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the possibility of libel
rubrics_metrics.description: Show how the writer obtains clearness and how he avoids the possibility of libel. (Paragraphs 124-131.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assert unproven wrongdoing; identify sources, use attributed statements when appropriate, ensure evidence exists before making accusatory claims, and avoid definitive language about contested motives or actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate tone for the story or lead
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the different tones of the following leads and the writers' methods of gaining their effects (paragraph 119); "The following stories... are lacking in tone. Correct them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a tone suited to subject and audience (e.g., restrained for tragedy, lively for society items). Methods include selection of detail, level of language (formal vs. informal), use of dialogue, and degree of editorializing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence details properly in a suicide story
rubrics_metrics.description: Put the following details in proper sequence for a suicide story: (exercise lists biographical facts, last actions, items left, financial background, location, time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange details so the timeline and causal background are clear: immediate circumstances and last actions first (time/place/manner), then relevant background (financial troubles, recent behavior), and identification facts (name, age, residence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid melodrama and ornate language in news writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and correct leads and stories that use overly florid, theatrical, or melodramatic phrasing (examples throughout chapters: ornate openings, inflated adjectives, sensorial rhetoric).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace rhetorical flourishes with straightforward factual phrasing; keep prose objective and avoid hyperbole that distracts from facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of antecedents and logical sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate and correct faults such as ambiguous pronoun references, muddled sequence of actions, and unclear subjects (exercises D and others ask for such corrections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every pronoun has a clear antecedent, sentences follow in logical order, and the chain of events is unambiguous to prevent reader confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specific identifying details (age, address, occupation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include necessary specific details — age, street address, occupation, relationships — to identify subjects clearly in news items (repeated emphasis in lead-correction exercises).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide these particulars when they add news value or help readers identify individuals; omit extraneous personal details that do not serve the news purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match lead style to publication/time (informal vs. formal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write for Friday afternoon's paper an informal lead to the following story: (exercise requesting an informal lead).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt lead formality and tone to the edition, audience, and context — e.g., a Friday-afternoon piece may be more informal; hard-news morning editions require more formal concise leads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dialogue, direct quotation, and vivid specifics to gain effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the different tones and the writers' methods of gaining their effects (exercise E includes examples using direct speech and dramatic detail).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ direct quotes or deceptively simple dialogue to create immediacy; use concrete, specific details rather than abstract generalities to produce vividness—while still staying factual and accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness in grammar, word choice, and idiom
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate and correct faults in stories (paragraphs 131-134) including awkward phrasing, incorrect idioms, and erroneous word use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise sentences for standard grammar and idiom, eliminate awkward constructions, and choose words that precisely convey meaning without ambiguity or unintended connotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide necessary context and avoid gossip/speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting matters that might be disputed (e.g., family quarrels, charges involving estate or reputation), provide context and avoid repeating unverified rumors (illustrated in the Myrtle Reed case and other examples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute allegations, document source of claims, give court or official actions as context, and avoid amplifying uncorroborated private disputes in ways that could mislead or libel.
